analyst_view.overall: Hamburg (12th) host Bayern (2nd) a week after a 4-0 Nordderby defeat at Werder Bremen, their heaviest derby loss in 22 years, and Miro Muheim (calf) is now out on top of Lokonga, Nadir and Remberg, though Fábio Vieira is back. Bayern are hit much harder: Harry Kane tore his ankle syndesmosis against Cologne on 20 November, had surgery and is out for three to three and a half months (confirmed by Bundesliga.com, ZDF and Sky), Michael Olise has a bruised forefoot and is doubtful, and Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari are also injured. Neither side's absences are in the numbers yet (no team news was included), and Bayern also play at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday. Bayern should still control the game, but without their main scorer and several wide attackers I expect fewer goals and chances than the numbers show.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, 2.8 of them Bayern's, but they don't know that Harry Kane is out for months (confirmed by several outlets) and that Díaz and Gnabry are injured and Olise doubtful. That removes most of Bayern's usual scorers; Hamburg's own absences (Muheim, Lokonga, Remberg) help Bayern a little, so I take 13% off, to about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Bayern will still have most of the ball and pin Hamburg back even without Kane, and losing wide players like Olise and Díaz could cut crossing a little, but Hamburg's 3-5-2 without Muheim may also concede more down the flanks. Nothing clear either way, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifting them slightly for past meetings and trimming for Bayern's calm recent record. Hamburg will want a reaction after the derby humiliation, but no referee is named yet and nothing points clearly up or down, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots and already add 14% for Bayern's high recent shot count, which came with Kane, Olise and Díaz. Without them Bayern should still dominate but create a bit less, so I take 6% off, to about 30.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target, 7.1 of them Bayern's. Kane is their most accurate finisher and is out for months, and Olise is doubtful, which the numbers don't know; I take 10% off, to about 9.6.
